source.title: SKIntern: Internalizing Symbolic Knowledge for Distilling Better CoT Capabilities into Small Language Models
source.authors: Huanxuan Liao; Shi-Zhu He; Yu-Pu Hao; Xiang Li; Yuanzhe Zhang; Kang Liu; Jun Zhao

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates downstream task accuracy for SKIntern-trained models at several Qwen2 sizes. This bears on downstream performance across scale, but it does not measure pretraining loss or fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. but does not test held-out cross-entropy scaling, predict losses from smaller runs, or find compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Rows below cover the Qwen2 SKIntern size sweep in Table 7; other reported results concern the proposed distillation method rather than these claim versions.
record.test_reason: A CoT-distillation method paper. Kaplan et al. is cited only to motivate small models. The Qwen2 0.5B/1.5B/7B sweep (Table 7, Fig. 4) compares the paper's own method against baselines across student sizes. That is method performance, not a test of whether downstream performance scales predictably. There are only three differently pretrained checkpoints, no fit, no loss and no prediction.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors conclude SKIntern improves ID and OOD reasoning accuracy while cutting inference FLOPs up to 4x across student sizes. They draw no conclusions about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates fine-tuned student-model accuracy on downstream benchmarks across model sizes; it does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit power laws or compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model size vary in the reported Qwen2 SKIntern sweep. The study does not examine sensitivity to scaling-law fitting choices.

fits_no_version.finding: After SKIntern CoT distillation, Qwen2 student accuracy rises from 0.5B to 1.5B to 7B on all seven benchmarks (e.g. GSM8K 30.9→54.8→76.1). The paper presents this as method robustness across sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CoT-distilled student accuracy increases monotonically with student parameter count within one model family.

record.problems: The relevant size-sweep results are downstream benchmark accuracies for one training method, not pretraining losses; no predictive fit, held-out size prediction, or uncertainty estimates are given for the Table 7 size-sweep values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on a claim version were left out. Table 7 results for other methods and the paper's other model families are method comparisons or do not provide a same-family SKIntern size sweep for the downstream scale comparison.

untested.parts: All. No pretraining loss is measured.
All. No extrapolation from small runs.
All. No scaling-law form is fitted in any regime.
All. No predictive relation between scale or loss and downstream accuracy; the size sweep only serves method comparison.
All. No exponents or fitting choices are compared.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' label is dropped. The rows are the paper's own method scores used to compare methods. The sizes are separately pretrained Qwen2 checkpoints fine-tuned with LoRA and different learning rates. With three points and no fit, the sweep cannot show predictability.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; bottleneck conditions; power-law fits over several orders of magnitude.
No loss predictions from smaller runs or comparison with larger-run held-out losses.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep, compute-optimal parameter/token counts, or fitted growth trends.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No scaling-law tests in other modalities or training regimes.
The paper reports benchmark accuracy across model sizes, but does not fit a predictive relationship, evaluate prediction on held-out sizes, or relate accuracy to pretraining loss.
No comparison of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices, and no test of curves bending away from power laws.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Qwen2 SKIntern models from 0.5B to 7B across the seven reported benchmark datasets
reader_labels.reason: For each dataset, reported accuracy increases at both larger tested sizes; rows r8-r21 show the increases against the next smaller size. This is evidence of improving downstream accuracy with scale in this setting, not a fitted predictive law.
